body:
A box mod is a battery unit, usually rectangular, that powers a refillable tank. It is the most adjustable and most powerful kind of vape device, and it is the heart of the "advanced" side of vaping: adjustable wattage, temperature settings, removable batteries and a screen that shows what is going on. It is also the device that needs the most knowledge to use responsibly, because the batteries can deliver high currents and the coils range across a wide spread of resistance. This guide explains what a box mod is, how it works, what the main features mean, how it differs from pods and disposables, who it suits, how to choose a mod and a tank, how to use it, how to look after it, what the safety points are with batteries and what to avoid. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice. Always follow the manufacturer's instructions.

## What a box mod is
The name "mod" comes from "modification", from the early days when hobbyists modified devices. A box mod houses one or two removable batteries, an electronic chip, a screen and buttons, and has a 510 connector on top, to which a tank screws. The chip regulates the power sent to the coil, so that you can choose wattage, and sometimes voltage or temperature. See [parts of a vape](/blog/parts-of-a-vape-glossary/) for the 510 connector.

## How it works
When you press the fire button, the chip draws current from the batteries, regulates it to your chosen power and sends it to the coil in the tank. The coil heats liquid held in cotton, and you inhale vapor. The screen shows battery level, wattage, coil resistance and sometimes puff counts. Protection circuits guard against short circuits, overheating and low battery. See [how does a vape work](/blog/how-does-a-vape-work/).

## Key features
- **Adjustable wattage:** you set the power, within the mod's range and the coil's recommended range.
- **Removable batteries:** usually 18650 or 21700 cells, which you charge outside the device or inside it.
- **Single or dual battery:** dual-battery mods give more power and longer life.
- **A screen and menu:** show settings, and let you adjust them.
- **Modes:** power mode, temperature control, bypass and others on some devices.
- **Protections:** short-circuit, overheat, low-voltage and reverse-polarity protection.
- **Size:** from compact single-battery mods to large dual-battery ones.

## Box mod versus pod and disposable
A disposable is sealed and fixed. A pod system is compact and simple, with fixed power. A box mod is adjustable, larger and more powerful, with refillable tanks and replaceable coils. It suits people who want to tune power and airflow, use sub-ohm coils and make large vapor, and who are comfortable learning about batteries and coils. See [disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/) and [sub-ohm vs mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/).

## Who it suits
People who enjoy tinkering, who want big vapor, who want to choose their coils and liquids, who vape regularly and who are happy to maintain a device. It does not suit people who want zero fuss. If you are a beginner, start simpler. See [best vapes for beginners](/blog/best-vapes-for-beginners-21-plus/).

## Choosing a box mod
- **Battery type and number:** single 18650 for compact, dual for power.
- **Maximum power:** enough for your coils, with margin.
- **Build quality and brand:** choose a reputable maker with good support.
- **Screen and controls:** easy to read and use.
- **Protections:** a full set.
- **Size and weight:** comfortable to carry.
- **Compatibility:** a 510 connector, and a tank that fits.

## Choosing a tank
A tank is the container and coil housing. Match it to your style: a sub-ohm tank for direct-to-lung, a mouth-to-lung tank for tighter draws. Check the coil range and the power range, and the liquid capacity. See [how to pick replacement coils and pods](/blog/how-to-pick-replacement-coils-and-pods/) for coils.

## Choosing batteries
Use batteries from reputable sources, with a continuous discharge rating well above what your coil draws. Never mix brands, ages or charge levels in a dual-battery mod. Check the wraps for damage, and replace any with tears. Do not carry loose batteries in a pocket; use a case. See [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/). If you are unsure about electrical details, ask for help or choose a simpler device.

## Setting up a mod
1. Charge the batteries in a proper charger, on a hard surface, while you are nearby.
2. Insert them with the correct polarity.
3. Screw the tank on firmly.
4. Prime the coil, and fill the tank.
5. Set power at the low end of the coil's range.
6. Take gentle puffs, then adjust.

See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/) and [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## Looking after a mod
Keep it clean and dry. Wipe the 510 connector and the battery contacts with a dry cotton bud. Do not wet the electronics. Store it upright, cool and away from children and pets. Check batteries and wraps often. Do not leave a mod in a hot car. See [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/).

## Battery precautions
High-power devices need correctly rated batteries and careful handling. Do not use damaged batteries, do not charge unattended, do not carry loose batteries with coins or keys and do not use a mod with a coil below its minimum resistance. Stop using any device that is hot, swollen or leaking. If a battery smokes or burns, move away and call emergency services.

## Traveling with a mod
Devices and spare batteries must travel in carry-on baggage, switched off, with batteries in a case, and you may not use them on board. See [traveling with vapes](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/).

## Common mistakes
- **Choosing a mod before learning the basics.**
- **Using underrated batteries.**
- **Mixing batteries.**
- **Running too much power for the coil.**
- **Ignoring wraps and damage.**
- **Leaving batteries charging unattended.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do I need to know electronics?
A little. Our guide to ohms, watts and volts covers the basics.

### What batteries do I need?
Reputable cells, of the size the mod uses, with a suitable discharge rating.

### Are mods more expensive?
To start, yes. Running costs depend on liquid and coils.

### Can I use a mod for salts?
Mods are designed for freebase in sub-ohm tanks. Some work with mouth-to-lung tanks and salts at lower power. Match liquid and coil.

### Is a mod harder to look after?
It needs more care than a disposable or pod.

## Shop
Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Reading the screen on a box mod
Most mods show a handful of values. Wattage is the power you chose. Resistance, in ohms, is the coil's resistance as measured by the chip. Voltage is what the chip is sending. Puff count or puff time may appear on some. A battery meter shows charge. If the resistance reads zero or a very low value, the tank may not be connected properly, or the coil may be faulty. If it reads very high, the coil may be burnt out. Knowing what the screen shows turns the mod from a black box into an instrument. See [understanding vape device indicator lights](/blog/understanding-vape-device-indicator-lights/) for the messages that appear.

## Starting power
As a rule, use the low end of the coil's stated range, and increase in small steps. If the coil is rated 40 to 60 watts, begin near 40. Take a puff, and note the warmth and flavor. Increase by a couple of watts until the flavor is full but the vapor is not too hot. Do not exceed the maximum. Higher power uses batteries faster, burns liquid faster and shortens coil life. Many people settle in the lower third of the range.

## Cost of ownership
A starter mod and tank set may cost more than a few disposables, but the running costs can be lower. Typical consumables are liquid, coils and batteries. A coil may last one to two weeks, a bottle of liquid a few weeks to a month, and batteries a year or more with proper care. Add the cost of a charger if the mod does not charge cells internally. Compare the total per month with a disposable habit, as shown in [how to compare vape prices per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/), before deciding.

## Mistakes to avoid when starting
Do not buy a mod because it looks impressive. Do not buy the highest power available, because you will rarely use it. Do not buy cheap, unbranded batteries. Do not skip reading the manual, which explains the lock sequence, the menu and the protections. Do not experiment with unfamiliar coil builds. Keep it simple, and add complexity only when you understand the basics.

## Getting help
If you are unsure which mod or tank to choose, or you are not confident about battery safety, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with what you want to do. We will point you to simpler products if that is the better fit.

## One more precaution
Before every session, glance at the batteries and the tank. A torn wrap, a dented cell or a leaking tank is a reason to stop and fix the problem first. A minute of checking prevents most problems with mods, and it is a habit that experienced users keep.

faq.a: A rectangular battery unit with removable batteries, adjustable power and a screen that powers a refillable tank through a 510 connector.

faq.q: Who is a box mod for?
faq.a: People who want adjustable power and airflow, large vapor and are comfortable learning about coils and batteries. Beginners should start simpler.
Usually removable 18650 or 21700 cells. Use reputable cells with a suitable discharge rating, and never mix brands, ages or charge levels.

faq.q: How do I set it up?
faq.a: Charge the batteries, insert them correctly, screw on the tank, prime the coil, fill the tank, set low power and take gentle puffs.
Use correctly rated batteries, never leave them charging unattended, keep them away from coins and keys and stop using any hot or swollen device.

faq.q: Can I take a mod on a plane?
faq.a: In carry-on, switched off, with batteries in a case. You may not use it on board.
